article.title: Software Ideas Modeler 15.51 – UML State Machine Project Loading Fix
article.annotation: Software Ideas Modeler 15.51 is a hotfix release that resolves an issue affecting the loading of projects containing UML State Machine diagrams. Updating is recommended for users working with these diagrams.

article.title: Mind-Map Collapse & Expand
article.annotation: This quick-reference explains how to use the Expand / Collapse button on a Mind-Map node’s context bar in Software Ideas Modeler to reveal or hide just the next level of topics. It also highlights how the default Auto-layout instantly tidies the diagram after each toggle, so even large maps stay organized with minimal effort.

article.title: Diagram Simulation
article.annotation: This tutorial shows how to run stochastic simulations on Flowcharts and Activity Diagrams. It explains the Simulation and Simulation Variables sidebars, how to set fixed vs. variable time/costs, resources, and connector probabilities, and how to tune runs, max steps, and animation. You’ll learn to play a single run with highlighted steps, execute multi-run simulations, interpret the results grid, and export outcomes. The guide also covers value syntax (constants, normal—bounded/unbounded, uniform) and variable sets.

article.title: Calculation Diagram
article.annotation: Unify spreadsheets, graph-based formulas, and AI insights in one living model.

article.title: Highlighting Referenced Elements in Screen Flow Diagrams
article.annotation: This tutorial shows how to visually emphasize (highlight) the element a Flow connector refers to in a Screen Flow diagram.
article.keywords: screen flow diagram;screen flows;wireframes;ui design;ux design;tips

article.title: Git Sidebar
article.annotation: The Git sidebar allows you to easily manage Git repositories directly within Software Ideas Modeler.

article.title: Swimlane Diagram
article.annotation: In the realm of process mapping and workflow visualization, the swimlane diagram stands out as a powerful tool for organizing and clarifying complex processes. This diagrammatic technique helps to separate tasks, responsibilities, and processes into distinct lanes, typically representing different departments, roles, or systems within an organization.

article.title: Navigation Sidebar
article.annotation: The Navigation sidebar in Software Ideas Modeler is a useful tool for searching and locating specific text within your project. In this tutorial, we'll explore how to access and use this sidebar to enhance your workflow.

article.title: Adding Messages to Lifelines Using Drag & Drop
article.annotation: Software Ideas Modeler provides a variety of intuitive tools to simplify the editing of sequence diagrams. One of the quickest methods to add a message arrow between two neighboring lifelines is by using the drag-and-drop feature. This guide will show you how to efficiently use this technique.

article.title: How to Create a UML Package Diagram
article.annotation: In this tutorial, we’ll guide you step-by-step through creating a UML Package Diagram using Software Ideas Modeler.

article.title: Customizing Scrollbar (Wireframing)
article.annotation: This tutorial explains how to customize the scrollbar element in Software Ideas Modeler for UI wireframing. Learn how to adjust padding, rounding, and button sizing to create a tailored scrollbar style. Follow these steps to enhance the visual consistency and functionality of your interface designs.

article.title: Setting Behaviors for State Actions in UML State Machine Diagram
article.annotation: In Software Ideas Modeler, you can assign specific behaviors to a state, making it respond with Entry, Do, and Exit actions. These behaviors dictate what activities the state performs when it’s entered, during its execution, and when it exits.

article.title: Software Ideas Server Setup
article.annotation: Server provides support for user cooperation, global repository and tasks.

article.title: Translate Diagrams - Creating New Translations for Diagram Elements
article.annotation: Software Ideas Modeler offers a unique feature to automatically translate the names of elements in a diagram using the power of generative AI (using OpenAI API). This feature is especially useful when working on projects that cater to a global audience or when collaborating with multinational teams.

article.title: How to Create a Data Flow Diagram (DFD): Step-by-Step Guide
article.annotation: In this tutorial, we'll guide you through creating a Data Flow Diagram (DFD) for an Online Book Store using Software Ideas Modeler. A DFD visually represents the flow of data in a system, making it easier to understand processes and data interactions.
article.keywords: dfd;context diagram;dfd levels;diagramming;tutorial;process modeling;online book store

article.title: Wireframes with Data Model
article.annotation: Wireframes are a powerful tool for designing user interfaces, and when combined with data models, they become even more functional and dynamic. Software Ideas Modeler allows you to bind wireframe elements to data from other diagrams, such as UML or ERD (Entity-Relationship Diagram), ensuring consistency between the data model and the user interface.

article.title: How to Create a UML Class Diagram
article.annotation: A step-by-step guide on creating a UML class diagram using Software Ideas Modeler. This tutorial will walk you through the process of building a comprehensive class diagram, including adding classes, attributes, operations, and defining relationships.
article.keywords: uml class diagram;how to;tutorial;video tutorial;class diagram;uml;diagramming

article.title: How to Create a UML Object Diagram
article.annotation: In this tutorial, we will guide you through the process of creating a UML Object Diagram in Software Ideas Modeler. We will use an existing project that includes a class diagram called ThemeSystem, which contains three primary classes: AppTheme, Color, and Font. This object diagram will represent different app themes, demonstrating how you can visualize object instances and their relationships in real-time.

article.title: How to Work with Combo Box Elements in Wireframing
article.annotation: In this tutorial, we will guide you through working with Combo Box elements while creating wireframes for your User Interface designs in Software Ideas Modeler. We'll go over how to insert the Combo Box, customize its appearance, add a dropdown, and configure other settings to fit your UI diagram needs.

article.title: Diagram Templates
article.annotation: Diagram templates provide a pre-defined diagram layout, allowing you to quickly start a new diagram with an existing structure. All you need to do is modify names, add or remove elements, and customize details. This tutorial will walk you through creating custom diagram templates and how to easily use them to generate new diagrams.

article.title: Quick Diagram
article.annotation: A simple and efficient way to visualize your concepts or ideas. Whether you’re starting from scratch or working within an existing project, the Quick Diagram makes it easy to organize your thoughts.

article.title: How to Generate SQL DDL Change Scripts
article.annotation: Changes made in the data model can be transformed into the SQL DDL scripts. Software Ideas Modeler allows you to generate ALTER and DROP scripts for your changes in the data entities.

article.title: Generating Example Data for ERD Entities
article.annotation: Software Ideas Modeler offers a nifty feature to automatically generate example data for Entity Relationship Diagram (ERD) entities. This is especially useful when you need placeholder data for presentations, testing, or early-stage development. The generated data respects the entity's defined attributes and their respective types, making the data realistic and applicable.

article.title: How to Create a Decision Table: A Step-by-Step Guide
article.annotation: Decision tables are a powerful way to model business logic and decisions in a structured, visual format. In this guide, we'll walk through the process of creating a decision table in Software Ideas Modeler, from adding conditions and actions to defining rules. Follow these steps, and you'll have your decision table up and running in no time.

article.title: Creating a User Story Map in Software Ideas Modeler
article.annotation: In this tutorial, we will guide you through the process of creating a User Story Map using Software Ideas Modeler. Whether you’re managing a complex project or organizing tasks for a team, this guide will show you how to structure your epics, user stories, and sprints efficiently. We’ll also cover how to manage user roles effectively by linking them as model entities.
article.keywords: user stories;user story map;tutorial;example;hospital management system;example;step by step

article.title: How to Create a UML Communication Diagram: A Step-by-Step Guide
article.annotation: This article provides a step-by-step tutorial on creating a UML Communication Diagram using Software Ideas Modeler. It guides users through setting up a new diagram, adding actors and objects, and illustrating message-based communication between system components in an e-commerce checkout scenario.
article.keywords: communication diagram;tutorial;checkout process for an e-commerce system

article.title: Deleting and Reconnecting Relationships with a Single Action
article.annotation: One of the handy features within Software Ideas Modeler is the ability to Delete and Reconnect Relationship. This feature is particularly useful when you want to remove an element from a diagram without breaking the flow of relationships between other elements.

article.title: Data Model Diagram - Visualizing Data Structures
article.annotation: Data model diagrams are essential tools for visualizing and communicating the structure of databases and information systems. They help stakeholders understand the relationships between different data elements and provide a blueprint for system design. Several types of diagrams serve this purpose, each with its own strengths, weaknesses, and ideal use cases. This article explores three prominent types of data model diagrams: Entity-Relationship (ER) Diagrams, Chen Entity-Relation Diagrams, and UML Class Diagrams.
article.keywords: data model diagram;data modeling;erd;chen;uml class;class diagrams;class model

article.title: Process Element - Modeling Actions in Flowchart
article.annotation: If you are looking for a flowchart action shape, you found it. It is called Process element and it stands out as the most used and versatile. Whether you are mapping out a simple procedure or a complex workflow, understanding the role and usage of the Process element is essential.
article.keywords: flowchart action;flowchart process element;action symbol;process symbol

article.title: OPT (Optional) vs ALT (Alternative) in UML Sequence Diagram
article.annotation: In UML sequence diagrams, the OPT (Optional) and ALT (Alternative) fragments are two important constructs used to model different types of conditional behavior. While both are used to represent scenarios that may or may not occur based on certain conditions, they have distinct characteristics and use cases. This article will explore the differences between OPT and ALT fragments and when to use each.

article.title: If-Then-Else using Alt Fragment in UML Sequence Diagram
article.annotation: Sequence diagrams are a powerful way to visualize the interactions between objects in a system over time. One key feature of sequence diagrams is the ability to model conditional logic using Alt fragments. This tutorial will guide you through the process of creating and using Alt fragments in sequence diagrams, including modeling if-then-else constructs and editing conditions.

article.title: Project Hierarchy (Day 10)
article.annotation: The models and diagrams are organized in projects. A project contains all elements, relationships, documentation, diagrams, other specific parts, and their associated data, fields and styling settings.

article.title: Drag & Drop in Diagram Editor and User Interface (Day 9)
article.annotation: Drag and drop is a very useful and intuitive technique. Software Ideas Modeler supports drag&drop actions wherever it is possible.

article.title: Editing Diagram and Model Element Properties (Day 8)
article.annotation: Each element is defined by its properties - id, name, style, owner, repository, associated diagrams, tagged values, documentation. and other element-specific properties. You may edit all of them using the Properties dialog and a lot of them in the Properties sidebar.

article.title: Styling Diagram Elements (Day 7)
article.annotation: Software Ideas Modeler offers plenty of styling options and settings. You may choose your colors and fonts, adjust the border width, the fill style, turn on shadows or gloss effects. An emulated handwriting style is also supported. It is possible to adjust the styles of individual elements. You may also extract these styles and reuse them.

article.title: Mastering Diagram Layout and Arrangement (Day 6)
article.annotation: A good layout makes a good diagram. Software Ideas Modeler provides a lot of tools that help you to create beautiful diagrams with a perfect layout.

article.title: Exporting Your Project and Diagrams for Others (Day 5)
article.annotation: The diagrams and models you created may be presented to the outside world in standard format files. You may print the diagrams, send projects via email or create the whole documentations.

article.title: Choosing Right Diagram Type (Day 4)
article.annotation: Software Ideas Modeler is a diagramming software which supports plenty of diagram types and standards. However, what diagram should be used in the given scenario? What diagram would be most useful for the specific task?

article.title: Basic Diagramming Operations (Day 3)
article.annotation: If you want to create models and diagrams, you need to handle the basic diagramming operation - selecting elements, renaming them, mastering the work with the clipboard to copy and paste the elements. It is also good to know how to delete the diagram elements properly.

article.title: First Steps with Software Ideas Modeler (Day 1)
article.annotation: This tutorial will show you how to start with Software Ideas Modeler, how to create a new project, save it and open the existing ones. It describes the main user interface layout and its components.

article.title: Drawing Diagrams - How to Draw Diagrams (Day 2)
article.annotation: The key activity in Software Ideas Modeler you would like to master is diagramming. This tutorial shows how to grasp basic concepts and how easy it is to create diagrams.
